safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of neck stiffness (or lack thereof) appears in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: For an acute, severe/unusual headache that woke the patient, documenting absence of neck stiffness is an important meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage screen; omitting it can reduce visibility of red-flag assessment and may delay escalation if later clinicians rely on the note. While the symptom was reportedly negative, lack of documentation can still impair safe triage decisions.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of fever (or absence of fever) appears in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Absence of fever is a key negative finding when evaluating headache for infectious etiologies (e.g., meningitis) and helps risk-stratify urgency; omission may lead to unnecessary uncertainty or missed recognition that red flags were checked. This can contribute to delayed or inappropriate management if the summary is used for follow-up/triage.
